title: A catalogue part that is not in inventory can still be found
refs: SV-9160 (INV-06; V1 baseline 55767168; PRD 1.5 s4 Parts=Inventory - PO DECISION)
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type under a tab strip.
1. A part exists in the parts CATALOGUE named 'ZZAUTOTEST Airline Coupler Vernway', part number 'ZZT-77-3300'.
2. That part has NEVER been stocked - it has no inventory record and no quantity on hand.
3. Parts access: Catalog & Inventory - View.
custom_steps:
1. Open global search.
2. Type: Vernway
3. Read the Parts group.
4. Clear the input and type the part number: ZZT-77-3300
5. Read the Parts group again.
custom_expected:
Both searches return the catalogue part 'ZZAUTOTEST Airline Coupler Vernway'.
THIS IS THE HIGHEST-RISK DIFFERENCE BETWEEN V1 AND V2. In V1 every catalogue part was searchable whether or not it had ever been stocked. V2 searches Parts (Inventory).
If the part is NOT returned, this is the change a customer is most likely to report as 'I could search this part in V1 and cannot in V2'. Record and flag it - do not raise a defect until the Product Owner has ruled on whether catalogue-only parts are intentionally dropped from search.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the V1 behaviour recorded in the ShopView code baseline 55767168 (FetchDataQueryHandler.php:317-331, which reads the CataloguePart table). the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945) section 4 does NOT list the parts catalogue as a source - it names 'Parts (Inventory)' and indexes description, part number, tags, category, manufacturer, vendor name and bin location, so this is a code-versus-document conflict: Standing Rule 96 keeps the V1 behaviour as the default and Standing Rule 58 makes the conflict a PO DECISION ITEM. If this case fails, record and flag it - do not raise a defect until the Product Owner has ruled. Read on 13 September 2026.

title: Finding a customer by their name with the spaces removed
refs: SV-9160 (INV-03; V1 baseline 55767168; PRD 1.5 s7 keeps spaces for names - PO DECISION)
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type under a tab strip.
1. A customer exists named 'ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling'.
2. Customers access: View.
custom_steps:
1. Open global search.
2. Type the name with no spaces: ZZAUTOTESTBridgeportHauling
3. Read the Customers group.
4. Clear the input and type it normally with spaces to confirm the customer is findable at all.
custom_expected:
Step 2 returns the customer 'ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling'.
Step 4 also returns the customer, confirming the record itself is searchable.
In V1 the customer name was indexed twice, once as typed and once with every space removed, so a run-together name matched.
If step 2 fails while step 4 passes, record and flag it - do not raise a defect until the Product Owner has ruled.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the V1 behaviour recorded in the ShopView code baseline 55767168 (FetchDataQueryHandler.php:229, REPLACE(c.name, " ", "")). the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945) section 4 does NOT list a spaces-removed form of the customer name - section 7 strips non-alphanumerics only for identifier fields and states that for names it keeps spaces, so this is a code-versus-document conflict: Standing Rule 96 keeps the V1 behaviour as the default and Standing Rule 58 makes the conflict a PO DECISION ITEM. If this case fails, record and flag it - do not raise a defect until the Product Owner has ruled. Read on 13 September 2026.

2. Type the customer's address line 2: Dock 7B
3. Read the Customers group.
4. Clear the input and search for the vendor's address line 2.

custom_expected:

Address line 2 is searchable in its own right, not only address line 1.
